Groups of axes of which exactly one applies to any patient

Source: R/nomogram.R
mm_exclusive_axes.Rd

An interaction makes rms draw one axis per level of the categorical partner, labelled sex (prior_uti=no) and sex (prior_uti=yes). The arithmetic handles it: mm_nomogram_points() matches every value an axis holds fixed, so exactly one contributes and the read-back agrees with the model to machine precision.

Usage

mm_exclusive_axes(nom, model)

Arguments

nom

An rms nomogram.

model

A mm_model().

Value

A list, one element per group of two or more mutually exclusive axes, naming the axes and the predictors that separate them.

Details

A clinician reading the printed sheet has no such guard. They see two axes both labelled sex and nothing on the page stops them scoring both, which is an error no check inside this package can catch because it happens on paper. So the groups are named in the returned object and in what it prints, for whoever writes the caption.
